# dope_solo notes — living doc. Read top section first (current plan), history below.

## CURRENT PLAN — as of Season 2, day 182 planning turn (21:00)
Status: **$100/$2000 left, 8/10 PTO, season score 0.0958, rank 14/34.** Cumulative
score is 0 (seasons 1-2 are practice, don't count) — so the real value of this
season is what it teaches for season 3, not the score itself.

**The critical finding this turn: budget pacing, not signal-reading, is now
the binding constraint.** Since d152 I did pick up booking frequency (11
three_quarter probes total + 1 overnight, mostly on the "trust the trailing
~10-trip ypa, don't get faked out by one zero trip" rule) — but the
doy152-182 window turned out to be a genuine dead trough (see data below),
so almost every probe was a real zero, not a misread. That burned $1150 for
one small hit (0.071 share, d181). **Net result: budget is now down to $100
with ~150 days of season left, including the single best window of the
whole year (fall day_1_5, doy300-335, historically ypa ~1.9) — and $100
can't even cover one $150 three_quarter trip, let alone a $400 overnight or
$550 day_1_5.** This is the real mistake to fix for season 3: don't let
cheap repeated probing in a soft window consume the budget needed for the
one high-value class/window that actually pays.

**Confirmed this turn — doy152-182 (S2) was a real trough, not noise:**
class-pooled ypa: three_quarter 0.053 (n=130 trips), overnight 0.037 (n=36),
day_1_5 0.032 (n=18), hd_am/hd_pm ~0.003-0.005. Matches (and starts earlier
than) S1's doy180-240 "trough" pattern. ONI this season has been steadily
warming: -1.57 (doy9) → -1.29 (doy71) → -1.06 (doy99) → -0.85 (doy130) →
-0.68 (doy160) — La Niña fading toward neutral. Whether that makes the fall
peak stronger or weaker than S1 is unconfirmed; watch fishdope/counts as
doy240+ data arrives.

**Rest-of-season-2 plan (d182-335, $100/8 PTO):** Budget is effectively
exhausted for the classes that ever pay (3Q $150, overnight $400, day_1_5
$550 are all now unaffordable except one single 3Q trip if a truly
exceptional signal appears). Only HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT are in reach ($80)
and those are **confirmed dead all season, both seasons, every window
checked** — do not book them on hope. So: default to staying home for the
rest of S2. Exception: if a single boat's trailing ypa clears ~0.35+ AND
it's a $150 3Q trip AND it's a free weekend (no PTO), it's fine to spend the
last $100... but $100 < $150, so in practice **there is no legal 3Q booking
left this season** — the $100 can only ever buy a half-day/twilight, which
are dead. Practical conclusion: rest of season 2 is observation-only. Use
nightly journal entries to log which boats run hot in the fall window
(doy240-335) purely for next planning turn's boat-list, since acting on it
this season isn't affordable. Don't force a bad trade just to "do something."

## FALL BOAT WATCHLIST — new this turn, from season-1 doy290-335 data
These are specific boats (not just classes) that ran hot in the S1 fall
peak — check if they're still sailing / still hot when S2 (or S3) fall data
arrives, don't just trust the class-pooled number:
- **day_1_5 (S1, doy290-335, n>=1 trips, sorted by ypa):** Ranger 85 (ypa
  5.0, n=4 trips/99 anglers — huge), New Lo-An (4.35, n=3), Pacific Voyager
  (3.74, n=3), Legend (3.67, n=3), Sea Adventure 80 (1.99, n=4). All far
  above the class-pooled 1.875 headline — the fall edge is concentrated in
  a handful of boats.
- **overnight (S1, doy240-335, sorted by ypa):** Cortez (2.25, n=9 trips —
  large sample, very strong), Ranger 85 (1.34, n=6), Sea Adventure 80 (0.66,
  n=6), Relentless (0.54, n=5).
- Note Ranger 85 and Sea Adventure 80 show up strong in **both** day_1_5 and
  overnight — worth booking on whichever class they're scheduled for in the
  fall window, not just picking one class in advance.
- These are S1 boat names; confirm they still exist/sail in S2's schedule
  table once doy240+ data is available (boats persist across seasons in
  this fleet, but always verify, don't assume).

## PROCESS LESSON FOR SEASON 3 (most important takeaway)
The single biggest lever is **budget allocation across the season, not
signal-reading precision**. Season 2 spent 60% of the $2000 budget on 12
small probes in the spring/summer (doy91-181) for a total score of 0.0958,
and has nothing left for the fall peak, which is worth an order of magnitude
more per trip (day_1_5 ypa 1.9-5.0 vs 3Q ypa 0.05-0.4). For season 3:
1. **Cap spring/summer (doy80-180) probing spend at ~$600-750 total** (≈4-5
   cheap $150 3Q trips, only on boats with trailing ≥8-10-trip pooled ypa
   >0.25, weekend/PTO-free preferred). Treat this as a soft ceiling even if
   signal looks good — the fall window is worth more per dollar.
2. **Reserve at minimum $1250-1400 and 6+ PTO for doy240-335.** That's
   enough for ~2 day_1_5 trips ($550 each) + 2-3 overnight trips ($400
   each) on the boat watchlist above, which historically outperform any
   amount of spring 3Q probing.
3. **Start day_1_5/overnight boat scouting by doy~250**, and start
   committing PTO for likely fall weekday trips by **doy~265-270 at the
   latest** (14-day PTO lead time is the real deadline, not a suggestion —
   missing it locks out the best trips of the year, as happened repeatedly
   this season with 3Q on weekdays).
4. Trust a rolling ~8-10 trip per-boat pooled ypa as the trigger (not the
   single most recent trip) — this part of the process was sound, keep it.
5. doy180-240 (and apparently doy152-182 too, per this season) is a
   near-universal trough across classes — don't fight it with repeated
   probes; a handful of cheap tests is enough to confirm it's still dead,
   then stop and preserve budget for fall.
6. HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT: confirmed dead all year, both seasons so far,
   every window checked. Never book regardless of narrative signal.

## Next planning turn checks
1. Did the rest of S2 stay in observation-only mode (no wasted $80 HD/
   twilight bookings)? If nightly-self found a genuine edge case (e.g. HD
   suddenly showing real counts), note what changed.
2. Pull S2 doy182-240 and doy240-300 class-pooled ypa once available —
   confirm/deny the trough extends as far as S1's doy180-240, and whether
   the fall ramp starts on schedule (~doy240) or earlier given the warmer
   ONI trend.
3. Check the fall boat watchlist (Ranger 85, Cortez, New Lo-An, Pacific
   Voyager, Legend, Sea Adventure 80, Relentless) against S2's schedule
   table once doy240+ is public — still sailing, still hot?
4. If this is the season-end planning turn: write up the season-3 budget
   plan explicitly in the top section (cap + reserve numbers from the
   Process Lesson above), since season 3 presumably counts toward
   cumulative and this is the last chance to fix the pacing mistake before
   it matters.

---

## Season-1 baseline reference (by class, doy bucket, ypa)
- HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT: dead all year, both seasons (~0.00-0.01). Never book.
- doy80-100: pooled 0.833 (spring spike).
- doy120-180: three_quarter 0.467, overnight 0.5, day_1_5 0.239 (second-best
  window of the year for 3Q/overnight).
- doy180-240: weak across the board (3Q 0.049, overnight 0.144, day_1_5 0.02).
- doy240-300: day_1_5 0.8, overnight 0.272, 3Q 0.122 (fall ramp-up).
- doy300-335: **day_1_5 1.875 (best of anywhere)**, overnight 0.184, 3Q 0.055.
  Boat-level: Ranger 85 (5.0), New Lo-An (4.35), Pacific Voyager (3.74),
  Legend (3.67), Sea Adventure 80 (1.99) — see Fall Boat Watchlist above.
- doy240-335 overnight boat-level: Cortez (2.25, n=9), Ranger 85 (1.34),
  Sea Adventure 80 (0.66), Relentless (0.54).
- doy335+: dead (season ending).

## Season 2 timeline log (condensed)
- Doy1-91: cold La Niña start (ONI ~-1.6 to -1.3), pier temp colder than S1,
  trips table flat 0.000 through doy91 despite S1's spring spike there.
- Doy91-152: mostly stayed home requiring multi-day/multi-boat confirmation.
  5 cheap 3Q probes (San Diego mostly): d100 (share 0.024), d107/113/127/148
  (zero). San Diego 3Q was actually running 0.396 ypa over its last 10 trips
  as of d152 — initially misread as "fading" off one bad trip.
- Doy152-182: booking frequency picked up (process fix applied) — 7 more 3Q
  probes + 1 overnight (Mustang), mostly following trailing-ypa discipline.
  Only one non-zero (d181, share 0.071). Turned out this whole window was a
  genuine class-pooled trough (3Q 0.053, overnight 0.037, day_1_5 0.032) —
  the discipline was sound but there was little real signal to catch this
  time, unlike S1's doy120-180 which was strong. **Net effect: budget spent
  down to $100 by d182 with the fall peak still ahead and now unaffordable.**
- ONI trend S2: -1.57 (doy9) → -1.29 (doy71) → -1.06 (doy99) → -0.85
  (doy130) → -0.68 (doy160), steadily warming toward neutral. Watch whether
  this makes the S2 fall peak run hotter or cooler than S1's.

## Open items
- Boat-level variance analysis: ongoing, see Fall Boat Watchlist above —
  keep updating each planning turn as new boats/data show up.
- No forum/submit_strategy tool available to this agent (solo variant) —
  decisions are notes.md + nightly briefing judgment only.
- Leaderboard: top agents (skeptic_solo 0.83, calendarist 0.70, etc.) show
  "books nothing" strategy strings — this is a solo-variant quirk (real
  bookings come from nightly judgment, strategy.py unused), not a data
  anomaly. Top performers are simply fishing more/more accurately on live
  signal *and*, per this turn's finding, pacing budget to have firepower
  left for the highest-ypa windows — that combination, not just trigger
  discipline, is what's separating rank 1-8 from rank 14.
